Modern.brandNameRationale: Bench is the working lab surface; Beaker is the fundamental lab vessel. Paired they ground the brand in honest lab work. Two-noun & paired naming follows the considered-modern biotech school and the broader paired-noun DTC tradition (Stella & Chewy's, Heath & Hound).
Modern.industrySummary: Modern biotech has split between the giant established players (Genentech, Amgen) and the technology-platform companies (Recursion, insitro). The opening is for a brand that talks about science the way a modern technology company talks about engineering: with clarity, with open documentation, with a clear point of view.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Recursion (recursion.com) holds the technology-platform biotech position. Insitro (insitro.com) sits in the AI-led drug discovery tier. Cellarity (cellarity.com) does the design-led platform middle. We sit closest to Recursion in posture.
Modern.positioningStatement: A platform biotech that publishes its work.
Modern.positioningRationale: Most biotech hides behind patents and press releases. The brand promise is that the customer (academic partner, pharma collaborator, investor) can see the science, the platform, and the pipeline without an NDA.

targetAudience.primary: Heads of Research at pharma companies, principal investigators at academic labs, and biotech-focused investors. They evaluate platforms based on technical depth and operational discipline.

dos: Speak in the language of the discipline
donts: Photograph models in lab coats with serious faces

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark only. Bench & Beaker in a tight modern grotesk, all caps, two words on one line. A small geometric mark, two intersecting horizontal lines suggesting a microscope cross-hair, used as the favicon and on every publication header.

colorPalette.name: Lab Black
colorPalette.meaning: Microscope housing, the dark of the imaging room.

Luxury.brandNameRationale: Three words. Cavendish carries the scientific heritage of the name (the Cavendish Laboratory at Cambridge) without claiming any affiliation. & Co. closes it as a small heritage firm. The whole name reads as a quiet scientific advisory house with deep institutional roots.
Luxury.story: Cavendish & Co. was founded by two researchers who had spent decades inside major pharmaceutical companies and wanted to take fewer clients, more carefully. The firm accepts a limited number of engagements each year. Most clients are second or third generation foundations, family offices, or scientific institutions.
Luxury.industrySummary: Top end scientific advisory has been consolidating into large consulting firms. There's a parallel market for small principal-led firms providing strategic scientific counsel to foundations, institutional investors, and family offices. The work is sensitive. The relationships are long. The customer is paying for the principals, not the firm.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Flagship Pioneering (flagshippioneering.com) holds the institutional venture-creation peer. Third Rock Ventures (thirdrockventures.com) sits at the same tier. The Boston Consulting Group's healthcare practice (bcg.com) does the strategy-led middle. We sit smaller and quieter than all of them.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A small scientific advisory firm serving foundations, institutional investors, and family offices.

targetAudience.primary: Foundation principals, institutional investors evaluating biotech, and family offices managing scientific philanthropy. They value the principals' judgment and the long relationship over the announcement of advice.

dos: Speak in the language of the discipline
Send paper letters where the situation warrants
donts: Photograph the principals for industry magazines

Luxury.logoDirection: A classical serif wordmark with elegant ligatures. A small hand-drawn ampersand becomes the firm's hallmark, used on letterhead, the printed scientific reports, and the wax seal of every paper letter.

typography.secondary: Söhne for the secure client portal

Creative.tagline: A biotech that publishes its experiments.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Petri references the Petri dish — the fundamental lab vessel and a real lab-vocabulary word. Project frames the brand as ongoing and exploratory. The definite article gives the proper-noun register of a serious research initiative.
Creative.manifesto: Most biotech brands sell the platform, the AI, the in silico discovery. We made Wet Lab because the actual work of biology still happens at a bench, with pipettes, with samples, with the dirty problem of life behaving messily. The brand is for the researchers who have not forgotten the bench, and for the customers who want to see real wet-lab data behind the marketing.
Creative.industrySummary: Biotech branding has been polished, AI-forward, and slightly abstracted from the actual science. There's room for a brand that's warm, character-driven, sticker-friendly, and serious about the wet-lab work that grounds every claim.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Cellarity (cellarity.com) sits in the design-led platform peer position. Recursion (recursion.com) holds the AI-platform tier. Insitro (insitro.com) does the modern-platform middle. We sit warmer than any of them, anchored in the wet lab.
Creative.positioningStatement: A biotech that talks about the wet lab the way other biotechs talk about their AI.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 50. Scientists, principal investigators, and biotech operators who have spent time at a real bench. Skeptical of in silico marketing. Looking for partners who can produce real wet-lab data.

dos: Show real bench data with real error bars
Quote the principal investigator, not the marketing department
donts: Photograph models in lab coats with serious faces
Promote in silico data as primary evidence

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark in a punchy display sans with the L of LAB stylized as a small pipette tip. Standalone pipette-icon for stickers, social profiles, and the back of every conference presentation.
